request.description:
Creates a new account in VERIFICATION_PENDING state.  
An OTP is sent to the provided email address immediately after.  
The account cannot be used for login until the email is verified.

Password rules:

- Minimum 8 characters
    
- Must include uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character
    

Username rules:

- 3 to 30 characters
    
- Alphanumeric and underscore only
    
- Case-insensitive uniqueness check
    

Client-side Turnstile requirement:  
The client must call turnstile.render() with action="register" before  
submitting. The token received must be sent in X-Verification-Token.  
A token generated with any other action value will be rejected.

See Human Verification → Human Verification Outcomes for token  
missing and verification failed responses.

request.description:
Verifies the OTP sent to the email address after registration.  
On success the account moves from VERIFICATION_PENDING to ACTIVE  
and can be used for login.

The field is named "secret" not "otp" because the challenge system  
supports multiple delivery mechanisms — OTP, magic link, push.  
The client always submits whatever secret it received regardless  
of how it was delivered.

OTP TTL: 300 seconds (5 minutes) from time of issue.  
A new OTP invalidates any previously pending OTP for the same email.

To reproduce:

1. Call Register Account successfully
    
2. Check your email for the 6-digit OTP
    
3. Set the secret field to that value
    
4. Send this request within 5 minutes

request.description:
These responses apply to any endpoint annotated with @RequiresHumanVerification.

Currently protected endpoints:

- POST /api/auth/register action: register
    
- POST /api/auth/login action: login
    
- POST /api/auth/password/forgot action: password.forgot
    
- POST /api/auth/password/reset action: password.reset
    

The X-Verification-Token header is verified server-side against  
Cloudflare Turnstile before the endpoint logic runs.

Local testing setup:

- Pass scenario: set secret-key to 1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA in application-local.yml
    
- Fail scenario: set secret-key to 2x0000000000000000000000000000000AA in application-local.yml
    
- Postman environment variable turnstileToken can be any string in both cases
    

Individual endpoint documentation references this folder  
for human verification failure responses.

request.description:
These responses apply to any endpoint protected by rate limiting.

Currently rate-limited endpoints:

- POST /api/challenges — OTP_BY_EMAIL + OTP_BY_IP
    

OTP_BY_EMAIL limits (per email address):

- 1 request per 30 seconds
    
- Max 5 requests per 5 minutes
    

OTP_BY_IP limits (per IP address):

- 3 requests per 30 seconds
    
- Max 20 requests per 5 minutes
    

The Retry-After header tells the client how many seconds to wait.  
The X-Retry-At header gives the Unix timestamp of when to retry.

To reproduce: send POST /api/challenges more than once within 30 seconds  
using the same email address.

Individual endpoint documentation references this folder  
for rate limit responses.

request.description:
Issues a challenge to the given email address.

Any previously pending challenge for the same email and purpose  
is invalidated first. Only one active challenge exists per  
email per purpose at any time.

type values:

- OTP — 6-digit one-time code sent to email
    
- MAGIC_LINK — not yet implemented
    
- PUSH — not yet implemented
    

purpose values:

- EMAIL_VERIFICATION — verify email address during account signup
    
- PASSWORD_RESET — verify identity before resetting password
    

Use this endpoint to resend an OTP when:

- The user did not receive the original OTP
    
- The original OTP expired (Redis TTL deleted it)
    
- The user wants a fresh code
    

See Rate Limiting → Rate Limit Outcomes for 429 responses.  
This endpoint is rate limited by both email and IP address.

request.description:
Authenticates with email/username and password.  
Account must be ACTIVE — registered and email verified.

Returns an access token (JWT, short-lived) and an opaque  
refresh token (long-lived, stored server-side).

All previous refresh tokens for this account are revoked  
on successful login. Any existing sessions on other devices  
are invalidated.

Client-side Turnstile requirement:  
The client must call turnstile.render() with action="login"  
before submitting. The token received must be sent in  
X-Verification-Token. A token generated with any other  
action value will be rejected.

See Human Verification → Human Verification Outcomes for  
token missing and verification failed responses.

request.description:
Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token  
and a new refresh token.

The old refresh token is deleted immediately on use — rotation.  
Presenting the same refresh token twice returns 401 on the  
second attempt. This detects stolen token reuse.

Roles are re-evaluated from the database on each refresh.  
Role changes take effect on the next refresh call without  
requiring a new login.

No human verification required — only legitimate clients  
that successfully logged in possess a valid refresh token.

request.description:
Revokes the refresh token and terminates the session.

Applies to all authentication methods — credential login,  
Google, and GitHub. Once authenticated, all sessions are  
managed identically through refresh tokens regardless of  
how the account was originally authenticated.

The access token remains valid until its natural expiry.  
Clients should discard it immediately on logout — the server  
cannot invalidate it before expiry by design of stateless JWT.

Silent no-op if the token is not found or already revoked.  
Logout must never fail the client regardless of token state.

No human verification required.  
No Authorization header required — the refresh token  
itself is the credential being surrendered.

Initiates the Google OIDC login flow.

This endpoint cannot be called directly from Postman in a  
meaningful way — it returns a 302 redirect to Google's  
consent page which requires a real browser to complete.

How to test the full flow:

1. Open this URL in a browser
    
2. Complete Google sign-in
    
3. Google redirects back to /login/oauth2/code/google
    
4. LoginSuccessHandler returns tokens directly LoginFailureHandler returns error + flowToken Client must call /api/auth/federated/register LoginFailureHandler returns error + flowToken Client must call /api/auth/federated/link LoginFailureHandler returns 403
    
    ALLOW_LOGIN — account exists and Google is linked
    
    REQUIRE_REGISTRATION — no account exists for this email
    
    REQUIRE_LINKING — account exists but Google not linked
    
    BLOCKED — account is blocked
    
5. Copy the flowToken from the browser response
    
6. Paste it into the Postman environment variable: flowToken
    
7. Proceed to Complete Federated Register or Complete Federated Link
    

No human verification required — Google has already verified  
the user's identity before the callback fires.

request.description:
Completes registration for a new user who arrived via  
Google or GitHub and has no existing account.

Requires the flowToken issued in the REQUIRE_REGISTRATION  
response from the federated login callback.

Flow token intent: OPEN_ACCOUNT  
Flow token TTL: 5 minutes — expired tokens are rejected.  
Flow tokens are single use — cannot be replayed.

The account is created as ACTIVE immediately.  
No OTP verification needed — the provider has already  
verified email ownership. This is treated as authoritative  
proof equivalent to OTP verification.

Returns tokens immediately — user is logged in after  
registration with no additional steps.

To reproduce:

1. Open /oauth2/authorization/google in a browser
    
2. Sign in with a Google account that has no Mathemate account
    
3. Copy the flowToken from the 404 response
    
4. Set it as the flowToken environment variable
    
5. Send this request with a chosen username

request.description:
Links a federated provider to an existing account and  
logs the user in immediately.

Requires the flowToken issued in the REQUIRE_LINKING  
response from the federated login callback.

Flow token intent: LINK_IDENTITY  
Flow token TTL: 5 minutes — expired tokens are rejected.  
Flow tokens are single use — cannot be replayed.

Auto-activation behaviour:  
If the account was VERIFICATION_PENDING — registered with  
email and password but never verified — linking a provider  
activates the account immediately. The provider's email  
verification is treated as authoritative proof of email  
ownership. No OTP step needed.

Returns tokens immediately — user is logged in after  
linking with no additional steps.

To reproduce:

1. Open /oauth2/authorization/google in a browser
    
2. Sign in with a Google account whose email matches  
    an existing Mathemate account that has not linked Google
    
3. Copy the flowToken from the 409 response
    
4. Set it as the flowToken environment variable
    
5. Send this request

request.description:
Sends a password reset OTP to the provided email address.

The account must exist — this endpoint does not silently  
succeed for unknown emails. This is a deliberate decision  
to prevent unintended OTP floods to arbitrary addresses.

OTP TTL: 300 seconds (5 minutes).  
Any previously pending PASSWORD_RESET challenge for this  
email is invalidated before the new one is issued.

Client-side Turnstile requirement:  
The client must call turnstile.render() with  
action="password.forgot" before submitting.  
The token received must be sent in X-Verification-Token.

See Human Verification → Human Verification Outcomes for  
token missing and verification failed responses.

After success:  
Check email for the OTP and use it in Reset Password.

request.description:
Resets the account password using the OTP received from  
Forgot Password.

The field is named "secret" not "otp" — the challenge  
system supports multiple delivery mechanisms. The client  
always submits whatever secret it received.

Social-only accounts — created via Google or GitHub with  
no password previously set — can use this flow to set a  
password for the first time. After success they can log in  
with either credentials or their federated provider.

All active refresh tokens are revoked after a successful  
reset. All existing sessions on all devices are terminated.  
User must log in again.

Client-side Turnstile requirement:  
The client must call turnstile.render() with  
action="password.reset" before submitting.  
The token received must be sent in X-Verification-Token.

See Human Verification → Human Verification Outcomes for  
token missing and verification failed responses.

To reproduce:

1. Call Forgot Password with a valid email
    
2. Check email for the 6-digit OTP
    
3. Set testOtp environment variable to that value
    
4. Send this request within 5 minutes

from the token, not from the request body.

no password previously set — receive INVALID_CREDENTIALS.  
They cannot change a password they do not have.  
Use Forgot Password → Reset Password to set a first password.

All active refresh tokens are revoked after a successful  
change. All existing sessions on all devices are terminated.  
The client must re-login after this operation.

No human verification required — valid access token
